items.score_basis: Adjusted EPS $1.04 vs $0.82 (+27%) with record revenue and FCF guide raised $25m; EPS range narrowed with midpoint up only $0.025 and segment margin guide cut to 7.7-7.8% from 7.8-8.0%, so a solid but not explosive positive. No consensus given in the text.

Record Q3 at 13% revenue growth with FY revenue and EPS targets raised and a 1bn MAU milestone; but ARR growth guide of 10.2% and an interim CFO/CEO handover keep the durable-growth debate open, and Adobe beats have often been sold. No consensus figures in the text, so a modest positive.

The CEO succession press release is dated September 3, five days before this 8-K, so the headline news was already public; the only possibly incremental item is the departure of the Creativity & Productivity president Wadhwani, a mild negative.
A retention/severance letter for the Chief Legal Officer tied to a CEO transition that the text implies is already known; immaterial for a company of Adobe's size.

Full-year revenue +8% and adjusted EPS +24%, but GAAP net income fell, a $7.8m rebate write-off appeared, operating cash flow swung to -$1.7m on inventory/receivable build, and there is no FY27 guidance or Q4 detail; for a volatile small cap the cash-flow miss likely weighs more than the adjusted growth. No consensus in the text.
A certificate of correction nullifying a charter amendment on Class E voting rights that was improperly approved; a governance housekeeping item with no economic content for common holders.
Effectiveness of a charter amendment removing Class E voting rights that was already disclosed via a June written consent and July information statement; no new economic information.

Headline op profit $211m includes a $161m net tariff-refund benefit; stripping it leaves about $50m against $103m a year ago, with merchandise margin down 330bp, AE brand comps -1% and inventory +14%. Aerie +19% comps and a comps beat on total are the offset; FY op income guide of $540-550m includes the one-off refund, so underlying guidance looks soft. No prior guide or consensus in the text.

An orderly CFO handover to an experienced external hire, paired with a mid-quarter reaffirmation of Q2 and FY guidance; the reaffirmation removes a little downside risk, and the CFO change itself is neutral.
A 40% dividend raise to $2.80 annualised signals confidence, but it is the fourth consecutive annual raise (so expected in kind) and the yield on a high-priced growth stock is small; mildly positive.

Record quarter: revenue +61.5%, EPS $3.76 vs $2.50, adj EBITDA margin 18.2%, Power gross margin 22%; but backlog fell to $2.5bn from $2.9bn with no new award announced, which for a stock priced on the data-center power pipeline caps the upside. No guidance or consensus in the text.
An $8.3m bolt-on in the small Teledata segment, immaterial against a company with over $1bn of cash and investments.

Revenue $52.4m 'on plan', but free cash flow turned positive, cash rose $76m q/q, non-GAAP op loss narrowed 33% q/q and bookings rose 73% q/q, evidence that the turnaround is working; Q2 guide of $51-55m is flat, so the positive rests on cash and losses rather than growth. For a heavily shorted, high-volatility name that is a meaningful up move.
Routine board appointment of a Class III director on standard compensation; no economic content.

Securities class action dismissed in its entirety; removes a modest liability overhang, though the ruling was three days old and possibly already on the docket, and dismissals are often amended and refiled.

Q4 revenue halved to $0.6m and net loss widened to $4.0m, with ATM issuance continuing; the CHIPS LOI of up to $30m looks already announced and is non-binding, and the NRE negotiations and Sumitomo deal are qualitative with no numbers. For a volatile photonics microcap priced on commercialization, a weak quarter with no new binding revenue leans down.

A CHIPS LOI for up to $30m is large against a microcap holding under $40m of cash, and government-stake headlines in small semis have drawn strong retail bids; tempered because it is non-binding, milestone-based, paid in equity issued to Commerce, and the press release is dated July 29 so part of the move may predate the 8-K's post-close acceptance.

Q2 revenue $108.1m (+13% y/y, record edge AI) and Q3 guide $115-124m, a midpoint about 10.5% above Q2 with gross margin guided up to 59-60%; plus a raised 5-year SAM and new channel deals. A strong sequential guide for a high-beta semi; no consensus in the text.
Annual meeting vote count: directors elected, auditor ratified, say-on-pay and an amended equity plan approved; routine.

Q1 sales +25% (+4.3% underlying) 'exceeded our expectations', gross margin +630bp to 53%, positive adjusted EBITDA vs a loss, and FY adjusted EBITDA guidance raised to $14.5-17.5m with sales guide held. A clean beat-and-raise in a thinly traded small cap.
Board appointment of an independent director described as representing a longstanding large shareholder; ordinary course, with at most a faint capital-allocation signal.

Q2 revenue +10% beat the high end of guidance, NRR improved to 97%, $100k+ customers +16%, non-GAAP margin up 300bp, and FY revenue and margin guidance raised; the offset is a Q3 guide implying growth slowing to 8-9% and margin dipping to 8-9%. Net positive for a stock where retention was the bear case.
The CFO additionally designated Principal Accounting Officer; administrative, implies a prior PAO departure but carries no economic news.
Chief Accounting Officer resignation with an explicit no-disagreement statement; a minor personnel item with negligible price content.

The input carries only the 8-K cover and the opening boilerplate of the earnings deck (history, long-range goals); the Q2 results and guidance themselves are not in the text, so there is nothing to size and no sign to take. Scored 0 for lack of content, not because the print was necessarily in line.

Bookings of $0.7bn (book-to-bill 1.4) and record funded backlog of $1.5bn, up 37%, plus non-GAAP EPS $0.59 vs $0.32; but revenue grew only 6% against a reiterated FY guide of $2.125-2.225bn that needs mid-teens growth, and adjusted EBITDA slipped y/y. Backlog supports the back-loaded year; modest positive for a high-beta defense name.
Ordinary-course board refresh: one director appointed, one long-tenured director retiring with no disagreement; no economic content.
A 13-year director retiring at the annual meeting with no disagreement; routine governance item.

Q3 revenue $29.6bn (+86%) with AI semis $16.7bn (+54% q/q), and a Q4 guide of $34.8bn (+93%) with AI semis stepping up another $5bn to $21.7bn at a flat 66% margin: sequential acceleration of this size is hard to have been fully in the bar. Sized below a small-cap reaction because expectations on AI names are very high and the text gives no prior guide or consensus.

Multi-year agreements extending Apple custom-ASIC supply through 2031 ease the long-running fear that Apple insources its connectivity silicon; positive but undisclosed in size and small against Broadcom's AI-driven revenue base.

Post-Calavo facility consolidation with ~$15m of mostly non-cash charges, stated as consistent with already-anticipated integration costs; routine integration step against a synergy plan already disclosed.

Adjusted EBITDA of $32.4m 'exceeded expectations' per the company, annualized Calavo synergy target raised to more than $30m, second-half guidance reaffirmed; offset partly by adjusted EPS down to $0.18 from $0.26 and a one-time tariff-refund benefit.
Progress update on a previously announced $100m buyback: 641k shares (~$7m) repurchased quarter to date; confirms execution but no new authorization.

No consensus in the text; EXXUA launch revenue up to $3.9m from $2.4m with scripts +138% q/q, ADHD portfolio up sequentially, positive adjusted EBITDA and $26.3m cash. Encouraging launch trajectory for a microcap, tempered by lower y/y adjusted EBITDA and full-year revenue down 13%.

Domestic comps only +1.6% with management admitting a difficult first eight weeks, and the gross-margin gain and EPS growth to $56.05 rest on 145bp of one-time tariff refunds plus 105bp LIFO benefit while opex deleveraged 100bp; low-quality beat, partly offset by commentary that sales strengthened late and should accelerate in fiscal 2027.
Closing of an already-priced $850m 4.95% senior note offering; routine investment-grade refinancing for a serial issuer, no new information.
Underwriting agreement for $850m of 4.95% notes due 2031, a routine debt issue by a WKSI that funds buybacks and refinancing; immaterial to equity value.

Strong quarter (revenue +13%, adjusted EBITDA +13%, leverage down to 3.6x) with full-year outlook raised again, plus initiation of a $0.52/yr dividend the company puts at a 5.6% yield and a buyback extension; a small-cap re-rating catalyst on top of a beat-and-raise.
Closing of a $500m 5.375% note issue for general corporate purposes by an investment-grade issuer; routine and immaterial to the equity.

Q1 'largely in line' with company expectations, full-year outlook (flat organic sales, organic OI -3% to -5%) reaffirmed, EPS +6% to $0.38, organic OI +4%, gross margin +40bp and FCF up $32m; relief that a depressed name held guidance, tempered by tequila and developed-market weakness.
Annual meeting vote results and an unchanged regular quarterly dividend of $0.2310; CEO succession already announced. Routine.
Closing of a $500m 5.375% note issue for general corporate purposes by an investment-grade issuer; routine and immaterial to the equity.

Q1 'largely in line' with company expectations, full-year outlook (flat organic sales, organic OI -3% to -5%) reaffirmed, EPS +6% to $0.38, organic OI +4%, gross margin +40bp and FCF up $32m; relief that a depressed name held guidance, tempered by tequila and developed-market weakness.
Annual meeting vote results and an unchanged regular quarterly dividend of $0.2310; CEO succession already announced. Routine.

Q4 organic growth 8.4% (second quarter above 8% after years of 1.6-3.6%), adjusted EPS +17.5% to a record $1.48 and gross margin up to 52.9%; FY27 adjusted EPS guide of $6.25-6.75, +18% to +28%, including the newly closed IPS acquisition. Small dividend raise adds little.

Closing of the previously announced $1.4bn Honeywell PSS acquisition, funded with ~$1.6bn of revolver and private-placement notes at 5.43-5.90%; closing and financing terms were expected, so little new information beyond removal of closing risk.

Revenue +26.2% with net retention up to 110% from 108%, $500k+ customers +28%, non-GAAP operating income $22.0m vs $6.0m and record Q2 FCF of $21.7m; a clear growth-plus-leverage beat by the release's own comparisons. The guidance section is not in the captured text, so the size rests on the quarter alone.
Annual meeting vote results and a charter restatement adding officer exculpation, both disclosed in the proxy beforehand. Routine.

Adjusted EPS $0.47 vs $0.35 and 'ahead of our guidance', Brand Portfolio organic +8.2% with 880bp margin expansion, full-year adjusted EPS low end raised to $1.50-1.65 from $1.40-1.65; offset by Famous Footwear comps -5.9% and below plan, with quarter-to-date comps only flat.

Diluted EPS +27.7% to $7.37 and EBITDA +17.1% against a full-year EBITDA guide of +8-10%, driven by a 47.8c fuel margin and inside comps +3.2% at the middle of the 2-5% range; guidance only held rather than raised despite the strong start, and same-store opex +5.0% is a soft spot.

CEO Julie Masino replaced by David Deno, ex-CEO/CFO of Bloomin' Brands and ex-CFO/COO of Yum; an experienced restaurant turnaround operator at a company under operational and activist pressure, read as mildly positive, with no financial information in the filing.

FY26 outlook raised to the high end or above on revenue ($3.27-3.30bn) and above the $120-125m adjusted EBITDA range, plus $77m of sale-leaseback proceeds for debt reduction and exit of the sub-2%-of-revenue Maple Street business, accretive from FY27; tempered by Q4-to-date restaurant comps of -2.5%.

Nasdaq confirms regained compliance on minimum bid price and market value of listed securities, which the price itself already implied; the delayed-filing deficiency remains open. Small positive for a microcap with listing risk.
Chief Commercial Officer terminated effective immediately with no explanation or successor; an abrupt departure at a microcap with delayed filings and listing deficiencies reads mildly negative.
Nasdaq minimum-bid-price deficiency notice with a 180-day cure period; the sub-$1 price was already visible, but the notice raises reverse-split and dilution overhang for a microcap.

Revenue of $116.1m cleared the high end of the $100-110m guide reaffirmed only a month earlier, adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $4.8m from $22.1m and opex fell 11-15%; tempered by 4pts of one-time tariff-refund margin, a Q3 guide of $105-115m that implies a sequential dip, and only $95.7m of cash. High-volatility small cap.

10% workforce reduction at a modest $6m cost, which extends cash runway for a cash-burning name, plus the quarter-end reaffirmation of Q2 revenue guidance of $100-110m, which removes miss risk; the Chief Revenue Officer's exit is a slight offset.
Annual meeting vote results and director retainers switched from cash to RSUs; routine governance with negligible cash or dilution effect.

Two-month maturity extension on a $2.0m B. Riley term loan and consent to a sale of the legacy Ekso Bionics subsidiary; small, housekeeping-scale financing amendment that only hints at the already-expected legacy divestiture.

Formal press release, with an NVIDIA quote, for a 50 MW GB300 AI compute deployment with Microsoft, plus new news that the partnership term is extended from two to three years. The partnership itself was previously disclosed and no dollar value is given, but a named hyperscaler contract at an AI-pivot microcap draws a large retail reaction.
Continued-employment offer letter for the existing CFO (salary, bonus target, 300k RSUs); ordinary-course compensation with no operating news and no bar to size against.

Q2 sales +7.3% at the high end of guidance, adj. EBITDA margin 6.8% (+90bp) ahead of the company's own expectations, and a raised full-year revenue and profitability outlook; the raise figures are truncated so the size of the raise is not visible, which caps the estimate.
Annual-meeting vote count; all directors elected, auditor ratified, say-on-pay passed. Routine.

Record Q3: revenue $1.67B +37% YoY and +6% QoQ, adj. op margin 22.5% (+1,180bp), adj. EPS $2.11 vs $1.64 prior quarter, growing backlog and a preliminary FY2027 outlook; the outlook numbers are cut off and no consensus bar is given, and an AI-optics name likely carries a high bar, so sized as a moderate beat.

Q2 results 8-K, but the captured text ends inside the presentation's cautionary statements before any results or guidance figure, so there is no number and no bar to size it on; scored 0 for lack of content, not because the quarter was routine.
Closing of $750M 6% notes due 2034 and a term-loan refinancing that pushes the maturity from 2028 to 2033; a debt refinancing with no equity and no dilution, most likely already announced at pricing.
Annual-meeting vote count; all directors elected, auditor ratified, say-on-pay passed. Routine.
An interim CFO retires and a permanent CFO is appointed in the ordinary course on modest pay; no operating content.

EPS beat (non-GAAP $1.15, +4%) and a buyback raised to $3B, but CooperVision is flat organically, a US channel-inventory cut carries into Q4 (CVI Q4 organic -2% to 0%), and the strategic review ends in 'actions' rather than a sale or separation, which likely disappoints anyone holding for a transaction.
One-year maturity extension of the existing $1.85B revolver with all other terms unchanged; routine.

Q4 adj. EPS down 37% to $0.39, organic sales -1%, 190bp gross-margin compression, and a 36% dividend cut ($1.56 to $1.00) for a yield-held staple; a new $500M savings program is some offset, and the FY27 guidance figures are cut off, so there is no bar beyond the prior year.

$1.9B all-cash purchase of ACV at a 45% premium, EPS-neutral in the first full year and accretive only from FY2028. It is small against Copart's cash pile but a departure from its organic model into a lower-margin dealer channel, which holders may read as buying growth; sized as mildly negative, apart from the same-evening results.

Q4 diluted EPS $0.35 vs $0.41 (-14.6%), gross profit -5.5% on +2.4% revenue, US service revenue down YoY, facility costs +7.7% and G&A +16.6%; a clear deterioration with no guidance and no consensus in the text, sized against the prior-year quarter.
8-K/A adding the compensation terms for an already-announced President appointment; routine.

Q1 revenue $479M (+9.6% QoQ, +115% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $1.20, and a Q2 guide of $525-535M (+10.6% QoQ at the midpoint) with a steady 68% gross margin; sequential growth is accelerating slightly, but there is no consensus in the text and an AI-connectivity name carries a high bar, so sized as a modest beat-and-raise.

Third one-week extension of the default waiver, now to Sept 24, with liquidity and collateral-covenant relief; it avoids an immediate default but the lenders keep the company on a weekly leash, and the explicit risk of a total equity loss or dilution in a recap weighs more than 'significant progress towards a transaction'.

Second one-week extension of the covenant-default waiver to Sept 18 while a strategic transaction is negotiated; staves off default but confirms the week-to-week distress, and the text flags a possible restructuring with a large or total loss to common holders.

Q1 retail units -81.9%, revenue -57.3%, gross margin 21.8% vs 36.6%, net charge-offs 9.5% vs 6.6%, cash down, and the capital structure is still unresolved; the capital constraint was already known from the June default disclosures, which blunts it, but the worsening credit and the depth of the collapse are new.

Q1 revenue +8.8% to $15.2M, oncology services margin 51% vs 43%, adj. EBITDA $671k vs $59k, and revenue up QoQ from $13.8M; a clean improvement for a thinly traded microcap, measured against the prior year with no guidance or consensus given. The $4.4M cash balance tempers it.

FY Q4 revenue +12% to $13.8M with services margin 51% vs 41%, but adj. EBITDA only $158k, FY adj. EBITDA fell to $1.6M from $7.1M, and cash is down to $4.9M; mixed, slightly positive on the quarter's margin, with no guidance.
A director will not stand for re-election, with no disagreement stated; routine.
The COO is promoted to President and COO while the CEO keeps his role; orderly succession-style title separation with compensation terms, no operating news.

Q4 organic growth 8.4%, gross margin 51.0% (tying the record), adj. EPS $1.29 (+18%); the FY27 guide of $12.10-12.25B revenue and $5.36-5.50 EPS (+8.5-11.3%) is steady rather than a step-up. A high-multiple compounder, so a clean beat with in-line guidance moves it modestly.

Against its own July guide (moderate sales growth, break-even to positive adj. EBITDA ex-refund, net debt near $5M) Q1 came in ahead on every line: sales +6.5% with bedding +13%, adj. EBITDA $566k, net debt $3.1M, FCF $7.8M. The Q2 break-even operating-income guide continues the trend; the tariff refund itself was pre-announced.

Q4 still loss-making, but sales +7.6% sequentially with bedding +12.5% YoY, and it discloses a ~$7M IEEPA tariff refund cutting net debt to ~$5M, plus a Q1 guide of break-even to positive adj. EBITDA ex-refund; for a distressed microcap the balance-sheet relief and the path to profit are the positive news.

Q2 sales -11.8% and comps -6.3%, in line with guidance; the full-year raise is only the $11.1M tariff refund and the outlook is otherwise unchanged. Management's 'July inflection' commentary is the one incremental positive, so it is sized slightly up.

Revenue +1% and subscription +3%, with non-GAAP operating margin down to 15% from 18% and EPS $0.11 vs $0.13; cRPO only +3%. FY guidance is 'updated', but the text does not give the prior range to show which way it moved, and the Q3 guide implies flat low-single-digit growth. Sized mildly negative on the margin compression and stalled growth.
Appointment of an independent director (Microsoft's Search & AI president) on standard director pay; ordinary-course governance.
Hiring of a new Chief Revenue Officer under Reg FD; a personnel announcement with no numbers.
Annual-meeting vote count (all proposals passed) plus a pay raise and RSU grant for the acting CFO; routine governance with no operating content.
Retirement of an advisor-to-CEO executive under an agreement already disclosed in February 2026; no new information.

Q1 EPS $0.40 up 21% on 7.1% sales growth despite one fewer week and 10.6% margin, offset by orders down to $191.8m from $238.5m and backlog down y/y; no consensus or guidance in the text, so sized modestly positive on the text.

Full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised from $0.28-0.38 to $0.47-0.52, a ~50% raise at the midpoint, with gross margin up 430bp adjusted and a positive Q3 start; comps -2.4% is the only soft spot on a small, levered retailer.
Closing of a $5bn investment-grade note offering already announced on 2026-09-10; the terms were public, so this filing carries nothing new.
A $5bn investment-grade senior note issue at 5.1-5.9%, mainly to refinance 4.9% notes due 2026; routine for a company of Dell's size, with a slightly higher coupon.

FY27 revenue guidance raised by $25bn to $192bn and non-GAAP EPS from $17.90 to $25.50 (+42%), on record AI orders of $60.9bn and a $95bn backlog; a raise this large beats even an elevated bar, but some of it will have been expected after the AI momentum.

FY adjusted EBITDA guidance raised from $28-32m to $38-42m, but the raise is smaller than the $16.3m of tariff refunds it includes; against that, ex-refund gross margin rose 490bp while sales fell 7.8% (DTC -11.5%), with sales guidance only affirmed. On a thinly traded microcap the headline beat and raise should win. Disclosure: the project instructions loaded into my context mention a DLTH trade

FY revenue, ARR and IAM-share guidance raised, IAM share of ARR up from 12.6% to 15.1% in one quarter, non-GAAP EPS $1.16 vs $0.92 and a 34% FCF margin; growth is still ~9% with about a point from FX, so this is a moderate beat and raise.

Closing of the asset sale to Progress announced in July. The only new figure is closing cash of ~$221m ($4.46/share) after adjustments, plus a vague mention of possible capital return. The text gives no bar to judge the cash figure against, so I scored it flat.

A Section 382 NOL rights plan with a 4.9% trigger, filed 40 minutes after the asset-sale agreement 8-K. Its own content is procedural. It confirms the post-sale entity will be a shell holding NOLs, but the move belongs to the sale filing.

Announces the sale of substantially all assets to Progress, approved at once by insider written consent. The shareholders keep a listed shell holding cash and NOLs rather than receiving a per-share takeout. The price is not in the excerpt, so the sign is low-conviction. It leans negative because an asset sale by a levered company that leaves a cash shell reads as disappointing next to a whole-comp

Comps -3.5% but improving each month (-5.7%, -2.8%, -1.9%), and adjusted EPS $0.05 vs $0.01, largely from a $4.6m tariff refund; cash fell to $20.1m from $33.5m. The board's opposition to the FullBeauty merger was already in the 09-02 proxy, so it is not new. Mildly positive.
Appointment of an existing consultant as Chief Growth Officer; an ordinary-course hire with no financial content.
A merger-agreement amendment that only moves the end date from Sept 11 to Oct 30, 2026; procedural, with other terms unchanged.

FY27 guidance calls for revenue of $84.5-86.0m against $91.1m just reported, a decline of about 6%, and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 1-2% against 15% (GAAP net loss). Q4 revenue already fell y/y and EBITDA halved. Positioning the reset as an 'all in on AI' investment year will not offset a guide this weak for a small-cap.

Sequential rebound (EBITDA $6.5m vs $3.1m), but adjusted net loss of $0.6m and EBITDA down 24% y/y despite $90 oil because of hedge losses; production down 4% y/y. Dividend kept at $0.12 and reserves replaced; no guidance to compare against. Slightly soft.
Closing of a previously announced $16m Midland Basin royalty acquisition that was already funded by the equity raise; the ~4.1x NTM cash-flow multiple adds some colour but no surprise.

Formal 8-K for an equity offering priced on Aug 18 and announced on Aug 19; the only new detail is that the greenshoe was exercised in full. The dilution is already public, leaving a small residual overhang.

The quarter itself is weak: revenue fell 29% and gross loss widened to $24.5m. The new items are positive: a first data-center capacity reservation for 75 MW with an upfront payment, a new target of positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 FY27, and $2.4bn of optional awarded backlog. On a high-beta story stock the data-center narrative should outweigh the print.
Legal-opinion 8-K for a prospectus registering the resale of up to 12m warrant shares issued in June; the warrants were already known, leaving only a minor supply overhang.
8-K for a $225m upsized equity offering at $21.00 whose launch and pricing were press-released on July 7, two days before this filing; the dilution was already public and the upsizing signals demand.

Record revenue of $23.5m (+70% y/y, +52% q/q), operating margin above 22%, EPS $0.41 vs $0.07, and funded backlog of $129m (+82%), with more confidence in the FY29 $150m target. The bar is high after a $57.50 offering, which implies a large prior run, but the size of the beat should still carry.
Underwriters exercised in full the greenshoe on an offering that was already disclosed; 260,869 extra shares is a mechanical, expected event with no new information.

Closing 8-K for a primary and secondary offering at $57.50 that priced on July 28 under a prospectus supplement already filed. The dilution and the Edenbrook selldown were already public; a small residual overhang remains.

Q2 comps +14.1% and adjusted EPS $1.68 vs $0.81. FY comp guidance raised from +6-8% to +10-12% and adjusted EPS from $8.65-9.05 to $9.83-10.31 (+13%), with Q3 comps guided at +8-10% and a new $600m buyback. A clear beat and raise, though the stock is already a momentum name.
A contained cyber incident on a single employee computer, with files exfiltrated but no PII, and management does not expect a material impact; a small headline negative.

The third credit amendment in about 18 months. It replaces the leverage covenants with a minimum-liquidity test until late 2027 and adds monthly lender calls, asset-sale prepayments and IP-transfer limits, which reads as covenant distress. The results exhibit is not in the excerpt, so the size rests on the amendment alone.

Q4 beat the top of May guidance on every line. Bookings were $1.5bn (3.3x book-to-bill) and backlog $3.0bn (+256%). FY27 guidance of $2.4-2.6bn revenue and $575-625m EBITDA (+86%) is described as significantly above the IPO forecast, and capacity is being added. That is a strong upside surprise for a recent data-center IPO.

Q2 adjusted loss of $0.83 vs $1.14, called well ahead of expectations. EPS guidance moves to the high end of $2.00-2.40, about +$0.20 at the midpoint, and Journeys comps accelerated to mid-single digits in August. Against that, FY comp guidance was cut to flat from +1-2% on Schuh weakness.
An orderly retirement of the Chief Strategy and Digital Officer, with duties absorbed internally and a consulting tail; a routine executive change.
Annual-meeting vote count; management slate beat the Radoff dissident nominees roughly 8:1, an outcome already public at the meeting the day before. Nothing new for the price.

Q2 EPS beat the company's own guidance on 440bp of gross-margin expansion, the go-forward portfolio grew high single digits, and full-year non-GAAP guidance was raised (to $2.20-2.30, ex Marc Jacobs). Offsets are a 10% sales decline and a Q3 guide well below last year; the prior guidance figures are not in the text, so the size of the raise is uncertain.
Routine $0.10 quarterly dividend declaration. The text gives no change from the prior rate.

Q4 adjusted results came in 'in line with company expectations' (adjusted EPS up 27% cc, helped by trade timing), and the FY27 outlook promises better organic growth plus a new $3bn cost-savings target, $750m of it in FY27. The FY27 EPS numbers are cut off in the text, and the large impairments are non-cash, so this is a mild positive with no hard bar to measure against.

Revenue of $46.6m beat guidance of $44.0m and FactSet consensus, adjusted EBITDA beat both, full-year revenue guidance was raised to $200m, and the company reaffirmed Q4 EBITDA profitability. For a volatile, recently listed small cap, a clean beat-and-raise supports a mid-single-digit gain; the raise is smaller than it looks because it includes acquisitions.
Routine annual-meeting vote count: three directors elected and the auditor ratified by overwhelming margins.

Item 4.01 auditor change from Grant Thornton to KPMG, with clean opinions and no disagreements. It carries the same press release as the CFO-change 8-K filed seven minutes earlier, so almost nothing here is new; a small negative for the auditor and CFO changing in the same week.

The CFO resigned effective four days later and was replaced by the controller, announced alongside an auditor change. The release frames it as a planned retirement with a 12-month consulting role and no disagreements, but a sudden CFO exit plus an auditor switch usually draws a small discount.

Q4 diluted EPS of $0.41 was flat year on year and down 80% from Q3, EBITDA fell 3% yoy and DTC new customers dropped sharply, with management saying 'market conditions softened'. A $1.00 special dividend offsets part of that. No consensus is given in the text; net, a modest negative.

Swung to FY net income of $0.24 from a loss, on 21% revenue growth and period-end AUM up 26%. Much of the profit is a $3.2m non-cash investment gain and the business still lost money at the operating line. The text gives no bar; this is a microcap, so only a small positive.

Q2 revenue grew 21% with record bookings and net ARR growth above 40%, but the Q3 revenue guide of $281-283m is below Q2's $286.3m, a sequential decline. Gross and operating margins compressed and adjusted FCF fell to $9.8m from $46.5m. A guide that goes down quarter on quarter at a growth software name usually outweighs the bookings story. The text does not give the prior FY guide, and it carries

Reg FD update that restates the Q1 consumption run rate down from 'nearly $20m' to about $15m after stripping one-time incentives, while saying it has since passed $20m. The metric is explicitly not material, but walking back a number from the earnings call is a small credibility negative.

FY26 ARR grew 19%, the company reported record sales and its lowest gross attrition, and Q4 non-GAAP EPS rose to $0.99 from $0.81. The FY27 guide calls for about 17% ARR growth, roughly 16-17% revenue growth and non-GAAP operating income up about 21%, a modest deceleration. The text gives no consensus; read as a solid print with a moderately positive outlook.
Ordinary-course appointment of a former AXA COO to the board. No financial information.

A definitive agreement to sell the International business (item 1.01) gives a levered name (4.5x net secured leverage, a December maturity still needing extension) a path to deleverage. Q4 also showed sequential improvement: North America organic growth, 230bp of adjusted gross-margin expansion and FCF of $58m for the year. The sale price is not in this text, and the unresolved maturity keeps the

Third straight profitable quarter, net income $1.7m, but it leans on $4.3m of IEEPA tariff recoveries (an expected, sector-wide event), with sales down 8.7% and 'no material additional recoveries' expected. The forward signals are the positives: backlog up 6.2% yoy and 8.4% qoq (Hooker Branded +34.7%), a stronger July ex-recoveries and the Margaritaville ramp. The text gives no consensus. The repo
Administrative rescission of CEO equity awards that exceeded the plan's annual share limit (about 78k shares). Immaterial, and the company states it is unrelated to performance.
Routine quarterly dividend of $0.115; the text shows no change in the rate.

Q3 non-GAAP EPS of $1.11 beat the company's own $0.88-0.93 range by about 22%, on record revenue up 34% and non-GAAP gross margin up 350bp sequentially. The company raised FY26 EPS and FCF, raised the FY27 framework (revenue +13-17%, EPS +16-20%, FCF of at least $5bn), guided Q4 EPS to $1.20-1.30 and cited a record backlog. A beat and raise this large is outsized for a mega-cap.
Scheduled dividend on the 7.625% mandatory convertible preferred at its fixed rate. Nothing new for the common stock.
Ordinary-course appointment of a former Booking Holdings CFO to the board.

Revenue grew 11.6% to a record, but Q4 diluted EPS fell 11% and adjusted EPS slipped to $0.85 from $0.87, with a 160bp adjusted EBITDA margin compression blamed on training and delivery-mix costs. The FY27 guidance numbers are cut off in the text ('continued strong revenue and adjusted EBITDA growth'), so the size is modest. The credit-facility extensions are routine.

Q4 adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $24.3m (9.3% margin) and FY26 EBITDA reached $94.6m. The FY27 guide of $105-115m EBITDA and revenue of $1.05-1.085bn implies continued growth, and Q4's run rate already approaches the midpoint. The text gives no consensus; a small-cap positive of moderate size.

Solid Q2: revenue and ARR both up 30%, non-GAAP operating margin of 21% and EPS of $0.20. But the Q3 guide ($514-516m, 24% growth, EPS $0.18-0.19) implies a sharp deceleration and barely any sequential growth. For a premium-multiple software name that tends to outweigh the beat; the text gives no prior guide or consensus.
Routine annual-meeting vote count: all directors elected, the auditor ratified and say-on-pay approved by wide margins.

The exhibit is a press release issued on 2026-09-15, with the call on 09-16, so this 09-17 8-K repeats news that was public two sessions earlier. On its content, Q4 revenue up 33% but gross margin down to 6.3%, $9.2m of credit losses and a walked-back cash-flow-positive target would read mildly negative, but little of it is new at t0.
The chief legal officer was also named President to lead investor communications, with no change in compensation. An ordinary-course management title change.
The co-CEO was retitled CEO of the North American subsidiary, leaving the founder as sole CEO. An internal reorganisation with no departure and no financial content.

Q2 sales 'exceeded our expectations', with a positive comp (+0.5%) after a first half down 4.2%. Underlying profitability was at the high end of the outlook before $13.3m of tariff refunds, and the FY26 outlook was raised. Much of the raise is the refund, which is being reinvested in marketing, and underlying SG&A deleverage persists, so this is a moderate positive for a small-cap retailer.
Routine quarterly dividend of $0.09, the same rate as the June declaration.

Blackstone disclosed ~$1.09bn of margin loans secured by collateral equal to ~54% of the Class A share count, and the company has agreed not to hinder foreclosure. That is a forced-sale overhang on a recent IPO and it changes no operating number, so a modest negative.

This is the first print since the IPO and the text gives no consensus to measure against. Q2 same-store sales of 2.3% trail the prior year's 3.6%, but management says they accelerated, guides Q3 comps to 3-4% and full-year adjusted EBITDA growth to at least 20%. On balance a moderately positive setup.
A routine post-IPO closing 8-K: the charter, the agreements, a board appointment and use of proceeds, all as already described in the prospectus. Nothing in it is new.

Full-year delivery, revenue and margin ranges are held and backlog grew for the first time in four years. Against that, net orders fell 12% despite 8% more communities, gross margin fell to 16.8% from 18.9%, and management says conditions have weakened since June. Net a mild negative.

Sales fell 6.7% and diluted EPS fell to $0.58 from $1.04. Backlog of $169m is down from $205m a year ago, though up slightly on the quarter. Part of the EPS drop is a compensation charge the company says will not recur, and management describes award timelines as extended. On a thin microcap that sizes to a moderate negative.
An annual-meeting vote count: directors re-elected, the auditor ratified and say-on-pay passed, all by wide margins. Routine.
A Reg FD investor presentation and speech for the annual meeting that restate already-reported FY2026 results, with no new guidance in the text available.
A voluntary recast of FY2026 fee revenue into the new geographic segments. The company states it changes no consolidated figure, so there is no new information.
A recast of the 10-K and quarterly figures into the new geographic segments, stated not to be a restatement. It was filed after the same day's results release and adds nothing to them.

Fee revenue grew 7% for a sixth straight quarter of growth, adjusted EPS rose 9% to $1.43, new business rose 12% and remaining contracted fees rose 14%. Q2 guidance of $860-878m in fee revenue and $1.30-1.40 adjusted EPS folds in AMS. The text gives no consensus, but the quarter reads clean and positive.

Revenue grew 60% and gross margin rose to 56.5% from 45.7%. FY27 revenue guidance goes up to $141m from $137m, about a 3% raise, on a quarter that looks to have run ahead of that guide. The adjusted EBITDA loss widened.
An annual general meeting vote count: directors elected and the auditor ratified. Routine.

Q4 revenue grew 66% with gross margin up to 54.8%, and first FY27 revenue guidance is $137m, 44% growth, a modest deceleration. The filing also carries a debt refinancing (items 1.01, 1.02 and 2.03). With no consensus in the text, a mildly positive read.
An 8-K/A that re-furnishes the same Q2 release the original 8-K carried three hours earlier. The amendment adds no new information; the news itself is scored on the original filing at -2.5.

Full-year identical-sales guidance is cut hard, to 0.2-0.8% from 1.0-2.0%, and Q2 identical sales were only 0.2% against 3.4% a year ago. Adjusted EPS of $1.09 grew 5% and EPS guidance of $5.10-5.30 is reaffirmed, which cushions the cut but cannot make up for a sales story that is stalling.
The appointment of a Chief Store Operations Officer from Walmart and Asda. An ordinary-course executive hire at a mega-cap, with no financial content.

Year over year the quarter is weak: sales down 4.5%, adjusted EBITDA ex-FX down 47%, and a net loss with a $3.2m goodwill impairment on LHD Germany. Sequentially it improved in revenue, margin and EBITDA, cash flow is better and tender wins are building. With no guidance to measure against, the two roughly offset.

Adjusted EBITDA fell 25% despite IEEPA tariff refunds lifting gross margin, and operating cash burn was heavy. Full-year guidance is phrased 'now expects' ($62-70m adjusted EBITDA, $0.44-0.72 adjusted EPS), which suggests a trim, but no prior range is shown. Q3 guidance is wide. Revenue grew 2.7%, partly on catch-up from the warehouse disruption. Net negative.
The President of Licensing, who was also CAO and General Counsel, resigned effective immediately, with no reason and no successor named. An abrupt senior departure at a small cap is a mild negative.

Management says EPS of $1.19 was below expectations and that conditions deteriorated during the quarter. Full-year deliveries are cut to 80-81k from 82-83k, orders fell 9%, Q4 order guidance is lower again and incentives run at 12%. The sequential margin gain and continued buybacks soften it only partly.

The same Lennar Q3 release as LEN; the Class B shares follow the same economics. EPS was below expectations by management's own account, full-year deliveries are cut to 80-81k from 82-83k, orders fell 9% and management says conditions deteriorated.

The CEO says the quarter came in below expectations on light lemon volume, and lemon guidance moves to the low end of its range. Adjusted EBITDA beat the prior year, avocado guidance is raised, a 30% avocado ramp is flagged for FY27 and a water monetization is reiterated. Mild negative.

Windfall Farms sells at auction for $15m in cash with no financing condition, which advances the asset-monetization plan. The price is low enough to trigger a further $4.1m impairment on top of the $9.3m taken after an earlier deal fell through, so the price disappoints and the certainty of closing helps. Near neutral, slightly negative.

Q2 landed within guidance, but omni-channel comps fell 1.9% and adjusted EBITDA turned negative. The headline EPS of $0.51 is almost all IEEPA tariff refunds ($0.86 of benefit), and ex-refund gross margin fell. 'Appropriately measured in our outlook' against a choppy category reads as a cautious or lowered guide; the numbers are cut off in the text.

Q4 revenue grew 74%, gross margin rose to 39.4% from 22%, adjusted EBITDA turned positive, and record backlog of $110.9m is up 197%, with $85.6m due within twelve months. Some of those orders were announced earlier, but this is a strong print for a high-volatility small cap with a defense tailwind. The text gives no numeric guidance.

LightPath sells its China subsidiary to local management for $4.5m paid over five years, giving up about $4.5m of annual third-party revenue. The sale leaves no China operations, which supports the NDAA-compliant defense story. The money is small and the strategic signal mildly positive.
A routine compensation filing: a CFO salary increase and the FY27 executive cash-incentive structure. It carries no business information.

Every FY26 guidance metric was met, adjusted EPS of ZAR 6.51 beat the top of its range and the company is GAAP-profitable for the first time. FY27 adjusted EPS guidance of ZAR 7.50-8.50 plus a stated ambition of 40%+ adjusted EPS growth a year is positive. It is tempered by a soft Q1 guide (restructuring), a Merchant segment that fell, and an immaterial prior-period error revision.
A special-meeting vote approving a previously proxied option grant of 1m options to the Executive Chairman. The terms were already public and the dilution is small, so it is routine.
The previously announced CEO, Heidi O'Neill, joins the board, and the bylaws get routine amendments for Delaware law and universal proxy. Nothing here is new.

Q2 comps -9% (Americas -12%) with EPS propped by $0.86 of one-off tariff refunds, and a Q3 guide of revenue -10% to -11% and EPS $0.93-0.98 shows deterioration accelerating; the full-year cut ('now expects', refund included) is the driver.
Departure of the Chief AI & Technology Officer with no reason given, while the company is already under interim co-CEOs; more management turnover, but a minor role and a bare filing.

Comps +2.7%, a beat 'across all key metrics' on the company's own plan, Bloomingdale's +11.3%, and the full-year guide raised on every line (adj EPS $2.15-2.35 against $2.00-2.20), with only about $0.05 of the tariff refund flowing into EPS, so the raise is operational.

Revenue +55% and adj EBITDA +69%, gross margin up sequentially, and new Kroger and Costco wins; offsets are no numeric guidance, gross margin still down year over year, and part of the growth is acquired (Bay Shore). Without a consensus bar in the text, sized modestly positive.
Annual-meeting vote count; all proposals passed comfortably and nothing new was disclosed.
The 8-K formalises a $100m offering at $18 that was announced and priced on June 29 and closed July 1, so the dilution was already public and priced before t0; there is little left to react to.

Q4 adj EPS $0.67 against $0.40, organic sales +21.5%, adj EBITDA margin 15.8%, and the CEO says results 'significantly outperform expectations'. The GAAP loss is from the impairment and deal costs, and the transition-period guide (adj EPS $0.66-0.76 for six months) has no prior bar in the text.

Revenue growth accelerated to 30% ('highest in several years'), non-GAAP op margin 24% against 15%, cRPO +73%, and the full-year guide was raised with the second-half raise driven by Atlas. Tempered by a Q3 revenue guide ($756-761m) below Q2's $771.8m.
Annual-meeting vote results and a charter amendment removing supermajority requirements; routine governance with no economic news.
Corrects a typo in the guaranteed-delivery deadline of the already-launched MiniMed exchange offer; purely procedural, with no economic content.

Revenue about 200bp above the guidance midpoint and EPS ahead of guidance, with cardiac ablation +88%. The raise is modest: organic growth guide +50bp, and EPS only lifted at the low end ($5.94-6.00 against $5.90-6.00). Part of Q1 is the extra week (~$570m).
Annual-meeting results: the incentive plan was approved, and the board rejected the resignation of one director who failed a majority vote over attendance. Governance only, with no economic news.

Sales +10% on data centers, but adj EBITDA fell to $13.7m from $15.7m, FCF swung to -$10.9m and SG&A jumped. The affirmed $72-82m EBITDA guide now needs a steep back-half ramp, and the revolver was cut. $400m of lifetime awards partly offsets.

Revenue collapsed to $5.6m from $9.7m last quarter and $13.6m a year ago, adj EBITDA turned negative, and backlog shrank to $4.8m, with management admitting a 'lull in order activity' tied to the Middle East. Only cash of $15.8m and no debt cushion it.
Annual-meeting vote count; the plan share increase and say-on-pay passed narrowly, but that is routine governance with no economic news.

Adj EPS $0.53 'above expectations', but $0.11 of it is one-off tariff refunds. Sales fell 3.4% on 'softer than expected demand', and the full-year sales guide was cut ($3.88-4.03bn from $3.93-4.13bn) while the EPS range was held only by counting the refund, so the underlying outlook was trimmed. Orders +3.2% partly offset.
Bylaw amendment raising the director retirement age; governance housekeeping with no economic content.

Sales +16% organic, 'ahead of expectations', with US growth accelerating to 13% and US new pumps +20%, and several pipeline milestones ahead of schedule (Fit FDA submission, Flex CE Mark). The guide raise is small (~10.5% from ~10%, margin reaffirmed), and Medtronic's pending exchange-offer supply overhangs the stock.
The General Counsel is resigning for personal reasons with no disagreement and an eight-week transition; routine officer turnover.

Revenue +13%, adj EPS $0.16 (a second profitable quarter) and gross margin up to 8.0%, but book-to-bill was 0.7x so backlog is shrinking, and the excerpt carries no FY27 guidance. Net mildly positive, with no consensus bar in the text.
The already-announced new CEO joins the board in the ordinary course; nothing new.

Revenue +35% and GBV +45% 'exceeding expectations', record signed GBV, non-GAAP operating income doubled, and the FY27 revenue and op-income guide raised; tempered by a Q3 guide implying deceleration to 30% and a wider GAAP operating loss. CAVEAT: the project CLAUDE.md loaded into my context states NAVN fell 18.4% after this print; I did not use that and scored on the text alone.
Adoption of an annual cash incentive plan and FY26 bonus payouts of about $1.3m to the named officers; immaterial compensation housekeeping.
Annual-meeting vote results plus officer-exculpation charter and bylaw updates; routine governance.

Revenue +30% to a record $2.03bn and non-GAAP EPS $2.58 (+66%), 'exceeding guidance on every metric', with all-flash +47% and billings +36%, and FY27 revenue and EPS guidance 'significantly raised' (non-GAAP EPS $9.73-10.03). An exceptional acceleration for a normally low-growth name; the FCF decline is the only blemish.

Beat 'across every metric' with revenue +29% and ARR +27%, and non-GAAP op margin improved to -9% from -20%. The FY guide is 'now expects' with no prior range given, so the size of any raise is unknown, and the GAAP loss widened. A volatile recent IPO, sized moderately positive.
Annual-meeting vote count with directors elected and the auditor ratified; routine.

Adj EPS $0.79 against $0.69, margins expanded, the Q2 price/cost imbalance is being addressed, and $42m of debt was repaid; but volumes are flat to down and the excerpt carries no guidance. Mildly positive, with no consensus bar in the text.
Regular quarterly dividend of $0.08, unchanged; routine.

Strong quarter (sales +22%, gross margin 37.4%, EPS $0.21 against $0.04), but the release and earnings call were public on September 9, two days before this 8-K's t0, so almost nothing new reaches the market here.

Comps fell 1.8% and the FY comp guide drops from ~2% to 0-0.5%, with net sales guidance cut about $50m. The EPS beat and raise both come from a one-off IEEPA tariff refund (380bp of gross margin) that management says it will reinvest in price, so the underlying picture is weaker.

The controlling holder cancelled his 10b5-1 sale plan and says he has no other plans to sell. That removes a known supply overhang and is a confidence signal, but it changes no fundamentals. The news came out on a Saturday, so it lands in Monday's session.

Revenue grew 30%, IaaS 121% and non-GAAP EPS 30%. Q2 guidance keeps growth at 30-34% and the full-year revenue guide is 'now' at least $90B, which reads as a raise, and the company says the new contracts add no capital need. The offsets are $30B of Q1 bookings, modest against the RPO base, and negative free cash flow, so I score it positive but not extreme. I may remember this event, and my rememb

Guidance is lowered, with adjusted EPS now $1.60-2.00 against $2.11 last year. The Q3 adjusted loss guide of $1.20-1.40 is deeper than last year's $0.92, and more Lilly Pulitzer promotions are coming. The Q2 beat is only small ('in line'), and the tariff refund is a one-off.

Q4 'exceeded guidance across the board': revenue +34%, nearly $1B of net new NGS ARR, and FY free cash flow margin 38.4%. FY27 guidance of 23-24% revenue growth and $4.16-4.19 EPS looks solid, but the text gives no consensus to measure it against, and ARR growth slows to 22-23% as the acquisition laps. I score it mildly positive.
A routine executive change-in-control severance policy and a housekeeping bylaw amendment. There is no financial information in it.

The quarter beat guidance on every key metric, with revenue +13% and ARR +12%. The text does not show the prior full-year guide, so I cannot tell whether it was raised. Net new ARR of $37M is modest, and a CFO/COO reshuffle adds some uncertainty, so I score a modest positive.
One director will not stand for re-election, with no disagreement, and the board shrinks to 10. This is routine governance.

The quarter was in line (revenue +10%, adjusted EBITDA up sharply), and FY revenue and EBITDA guidance is only maintained, not raised. The repeated warning about second-half variability in network solutions revenue tilts it slightly negative.

Q2 was a record ($116M, +58%, adjusted EBITDA $13.9M), but it was lifted by a satellite handover. Q3 guidance steps down to $101-105M with an adjusted EBITDA loss, and the text gives no prior FY guide to show a raise. On a high-momentum stock the sequential step-down more likely reads negative, but this carries low confidence.
The annual-meeting vote count: directors re-elected, auditor ratified and say-on-pay passed. There is nothing new in it.
This 8-K covers executive appointments already announced in an August 24 press release, so it adds no news and contains no financial information.

Comps fell 2.9%, the quarter swung to an adjusted loss of $0.27 from +$0.40, and adjusted EBITDA fell 24%, with no guidance to lean on. The claim that comps improved in July and Q3-to-date is partly offsetting and could spark short covering, so I score it moderately negative.

The CEO retired abruptly, effective the previous day, for personal reasons, mid-turnaround and about two years in. The CFO moves up and the CFO seat is filled on an interim basis. That leadership instability is negative, softened by continuity in the Back-to-Basics plan.

Sales rose 24%, adjusted pretax income rose from $4.9M to $8.3M, and backlog hit a record $142M with strong operating cash flow. Against that, gross margin slipped, a $3.9M customer receivable was written off, and the $67M of awards was already announced in August. On a thin microcap this is a moderate positive.
An $18M ABL is refinanced into a $75M revolver plus a $14M term loan from JPMorgan, with a $50M accordion. That is more liquidity for growth on ordinary terms and a mild positive for a microcap.

Non-GAAP EPS of $3.70 beat the $3.00-3.10 guide; the tariff refund was 'received as expected', so it was in the guide. The operating margin beat too, at 11.1% against about 9.5%. But the FY guidance is only reaffirmed despite the Q2 beat, which implies a softer second half, and the $439M goodwill impairment on 'geopolitical/macro' assumptions is a mild negative signal.
An unchanged, token quarterly dividend of $0.0375. This is routine.
A permanent CFO (Sephora's global CFO/COO) fills a role held on an interim basis since January. It removes a small leadership uncertainty and carries no financial news.

This is the first print after the IPO: revenue +24%, active customers +23% and adjusted EBITDA margin up 320bp. The FY guide of 18.6-19.5% growth implies some second-half deceleration, and there is no published consensus in the text. I score a modest positive on a strong debut quarter.
A mechanical filing of the IPO closing and the charter/bylaws taking effect. The terms were already public in the prospectus.
This only sets the record date for a $15M rights offering announced four days earlier. The terms are unchanged, so there is no new information.

A $15M rights offering of up to 4.2M shares at about $3.55, backstopped by the controlling investor group, is large against a small equity base with only $29M of cash. It is heavy dilution that signals a liquidity need. Pricing at VWAP rather than a deep discount, and the backstop, soften the hit.

Revenue grew 21% to a record, gross margin rose 609bp and adjusted EBITDA reached $12.6M from $3.6M, with FY guidance reaffirmed and a permanent CEO named. Offsetting that, ending active subscribers fell 3.8%, Q3 guides to negative EBITDA margin and cash is down to $29M. The rights offering is scored separately.

A record Q2: EPS $1.06 against $0.22, and core gross profit (excluding 45Z credits) up 144% on better crush margins and co-product prices. The EPA draft Class VI permits de-risk the carbon capture project. There is no consensus in the text, and crush margins were partly observable in advance, so I cap the size.
New executive employment agreements raise the maximum bonus caps, the CEO's from $5M to $12M. That is a mild governance negative, but it is routine and not material to value.
The annual-meeting vote results: one director elected, say-on-pay and the auditor approved. This is routine.

Record sales of $24.0M (+21% year on year, +16% sequentially), 160bp of margin expansion, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.19 against $0.10. Backlog is still growing. This is a clear operating-leverage beat on a thinly traded microcap, but bookings slightly below sales and the lack of a consensus in the text keep it from going larger.

Q4 revenue fell 7% and adjusted EBITDA slipped, with consolidated comps flat (+0.1%) and franchise salons down 199. Supercuts comps of +2.6% and the active pursuit of a refinancing partly offset that. There is no guidance and no consensus in the text.

Q2 revenue (+2.6%) and normalized EBITDA margin both beat the high end of guidance. But the 'updated' FY outlook of 5.5-7% growth leans on a Q4 hockey stick of 16-21% growth, $50M of unplanned oil-driven supply-chain costs absorb most of the tariff refund, and RH's back-loaded guides tend to be discounted, so I lean negative. I recall RH was traded around this print in the repo's book, but not the
Internal promotion and a Chief Legal Officer hire; ordinary-course executive appointments with no financial content.

Founder-CEO, historically a buyer, sold 125k shares (~2.5% of his stake, ~0.7% of shares out) for personal liquidity; his first discretionary sale since 2019, read as a modest negative signal despite the reassuring framing.

Q4 revenue +18.5%, adj EPS $0.15 vs $0.11, adj EBITDA +31.6% with 240bp margin expansion, plus constructive freight-recovery commentary and no net debt; no consensus or guidance in text, sized against prior-year comps which it beats clearly.
COO appointment on ordinary terms and annual-meeting date notice; no financial content.

Refinancing of an existing $200m revolver with longer maturity, slightly lower pricing and a larger accordion; company already has no net debt, so marginally positive and largely routine (press release dated two days before the filing).

ARR +25%, SaaS ARR +36%, RPO growth accelerating to 30%, FY29 targets reiterated; the text gives no prior guidance to judge a raise, and the Q3 revenue guide (16-17%) implies deceleration, so a modest positive rather than a large one.

Q2 comps -7.1%, gross margin down 690bp, EPS $0.23 vs $0.70, and full-year sales and adjusted EPS guidance lowered with a persisting promotional environment; partly offset by August comps improving to -2.7% and a debt-free balance sheet.
Execution of the $125m ASR already announced with Q2 results on 2026-09-09; nothing new in the text beyond the initial share delivery.

FY adj EPS guide raised to $10.45-12.15 from $9.20-11.00 (midpoint +12%), Q2 adj EPS $2.19 vs $1.61 on +2.2% comps, buyback authorization lifted to $700m with a $125m ASR; tempered because part of the raise is tariff refunds and credit-agreement one-offs and sales guidance is unchanged.
Single director resignation with no disagreement and board size reduced; routine governance filing.

FY revenue guide cut to $380-390m from $388-406m (midpoint -3%) on accelerating consumer pressure, Q2 revenue -3%; EBITDA and FCF guidance held, but for a highly levered name with debt restructuring flagged as top priority the top-line cut weighs.
Director resignation with no disagreement; routine governance filing.
Closing of the previously disclosed Global Knowledge sale for small consideration with pro forma financials, filed four days after the closing press release; no new information.

Third straight quarter of product-revenue acceleration to 37%, Q3 guide 37-38%, and FY product revenue raised by $230m from 31% to 36% growth with op margin lifted a point; an unusually large raise for a consumption name, though expectations into the print were likely elevated.
CEO performance PSU grant of 1m shares vesting only at steep stock-price hurdles; retention signal slightly positive, dilution modest and contingent.

Flat comps with 50bp gross margin gain, narrower adj loss ($0.08 vs $0.12), inventory -10% and net debt -$26m, full-year guidance reaffirmed; modestly better than a challenged prior year for a levered small cap, with part of the margin gain a one-time tariff benefit.

Record Q1 with rental revenue +12.5%, adj EPS +20%, and FY revenue/rental growth and EBITDA guidance raised (EBITDA midpoint +1.4%) with higher capex signalling demand; tempered by ~250bp of one-off World Cup contribution and EBITDA margin down 100bp.
Annual-meeting vote count; all proposals passed, say-on-pay ~75% support; routine.
Closing of previously announced $1.2bn investment-grade-style senior notes for general corporate purposes at 1.8x leverage; already priced, no equity impact.
Annual-meeting vote count, all proposals passed comfortably; routine.

Q1 sales +32% and EPS $0.06 vs -$0.08, EBITDAS margin 12.2% vs 8.7%, Q2 guided ~10% above last year; tempered because 260bp of margin was a non-recurring tariff refund and FY revenue growth is only reiterated at 5-7%, implying a softer second half.

Investor Day deck recapping FY26 and growth lanes (suppressors, professional, new categories); the visible text carries no new financial targets, so only a small positive from the strategic narrative.

Q4 sales -8.4%, gross margin -230bp, EPS $0.78 vs $2.36 and adj EBITDA -37%, with towable share still slipping; the deliberate below-retail production and healthy dealer inventory soften it, and the visible text carries no FY27 guidance to offset.

Headline says it beat its own outlook: comps +12.1%, gross margin +300bp, EPS $0.27 vs $0.10, and fiscal August comps accelerating to +14.6% with a first profitable year since 2022 in sight; a small-cap turnaround beat with momentum into Q3.
Voluntary uplisting from NYSE American to Nasdaq Global Market with upbeat AI/auto demand commentary; visibility story for a microcap, small positive, no financial numbers.
Bylaw amendment adding advance-notice/universal-proxy procedures and exclusive-forum provisions; routine governance.

Q2 revenue +21% (decelerating from 25%) with strong margin and FCF, but Q3 guide of $285-287m sits below Q2's $292.8m and Q3 non-GAAP op income of $29-30m versus $44.4m implies a sharp sequential step-down; no prior guidance in text to judge a raise.
Board expansion with an outside CEO elected as independent director; ordinary-course appointment.

Record Q3 with sales +8.4% and adj EPS +7.3%, FY sales growth guide raised to 6.3-6.6% from 4.0-6.5% and adj EPS to $4.60-4.65 from $4.50-4.62; a narrowing toward the top rather than a big raise, with Professional margin slipping 40bp.
Planned CEO succession to the internal President/COO, with the outgoing CEO staying as Executive Chairman; orderly and signalled by his 2025 COO appointment.

Delivered updated FY26 outlook (adj EBITDA +27%, leverage 2.2x) and guided FY27 adj EBITDA high-single-digit growth with midpoint $25m above the Investor Day bar, plus a new $200m buyback; sales still shrinking. No consensus in the text; project context notes UNFI was hunted for this print but gives no move.

Management reshuffle: CFO moves to President/COO, external CFO hired from Carrier, supply chain chief departing. Planned-looking transition with no numbers; small, slightly negative for a CFO change in a turnaround.

Solana treasury company whose value tracks SOL, and holdings were largely known; the results add a $246m net loss, stockholders' equity turned negative (-$53.8m) on $220m of debt, and ongoing ATM issuance. The one positive is that staking should cover cash opex. No guidance bar, so sized on the text; mildly negative.
Just announces the date of the earnings call. Contains no numbers.

The BitGo loan rate is cut from 11.5% to 7.5% on $57.3m, saving about $2m a year, and the collateral requirement is lowered, which reduces liquidation risk. It is modestly positive for a small crypto-treasury name whose price is otherwise driven by SOL.

Q2 was already pre-announced at the high end on 08-27, so the quarter itself (+11.7% sales, 48.2% gross margin ex-refund, in line) carries little news. The FY26 raise includes the one-off $10.4m IEEPA tariff refund, and Q3 guides +5-8% sales. Modestly positive for a microcap. Project context says the 09-10 run ranked several names on IEEPA refunds, but it gives no move for this one.

Surprise acquisition of the OVO (Drake) operating business for nominal cash plus a 5% IP stake, expected accretive in FY27, with a preannouncement that Q2 lands at the high end of guidance. For a microcap this is a high-visibility growth story at little cost, so positive.

Turnaround quarter: direct comps +9.2% with every channel positive, non-GAAP EPS +$0.11 against -$0.02 a year ago, inventory down 28% and cash doubled with no debt. Part of the margin is a one-off $7.7m tariff refund, and FY guidance is only reiterated, not raised. Project context says VRA was in the stage E book for this print, but gives no direction or move.
Routine severance agreements for the COO/CFO and the chief brand officer. The change-in-control kicker hints faintly at strategic options, but nothing here is material.

Clean beat: adj EPS $0.95 against its own $0.65-0.75 guide, adj op income $124m against $90-100m, comps +9%. FY adj op income is raised only $10m at the midpoint against a ~$29m Q2 beat, which implies a back half trimmed by stepped-up marketing, so the upside is tempered.
Ordinary-course board appointment (ex-Starbucks CTO) following a search disclosed in May. Contains no financial information.

Platform assets grew 12% but revenue only 1%, because higher-fee cash assets fell 4%. Adj EBITDA fell 15% with margin down from 49% to 41%, adj FCF fell 27%, and opex rose 17%; the release carries no guidance, and the $30m buyback and >$100bn AUM milestone only partly offset. Q1 was 'in line with expectations' and the FY27 outlook is reaffirmed, but adj EPS fell 10%, revenue fell 3%, Learning dropped 20% with EBITDA down 56%, and leverage rose to 2.7x after Emerald. Research +4% and $8m of cost savings offset part of that. Slightly negative against a reaffirmation bar.
Internal promotion of the global controller to chief accounting officer. The predecessor stays on until his planned retirement, so this is ordinary course.

Class B share of Wiley, same release as WLY. Q1 was in line and FY27 reaffirmed, adj EPS -10%, Learning -20% and leverage 2.7x after Emerald, with Research growth and cost savings as offsets. Slightly negative.
Class B share of Wiley, same filing as WLY: an internal promotion to chief accounting officer. Ordinary course.

Profit came in ahead of outlook, but comps were only +0.6% and sales flat, hurt by the membership points relaunch. The FY outlook is reaffirmed, not raised, and now includes a $6.8m tariff refund, which implies a weaker underlying back half, with Q3 sales guided to only +0.4-1.0%. The $75m debt prepayment helps but does not offset that.
Board swap in which the controlling holder's designee replaces a resigning director. The new director is an ex-TJX CFO who takes the audit chair. Ordinary course.
The chief HR officer is resigning for personal reasons, with a transition in place. Not material.

Sales +13% (7% organic), adj EBITDA +10% and free cash flow nearly doubled, plus a data-center liquid-cooling tank demand callout. But adj op income was flat even with a $4m tariff refund, Building mix was weak, and adj EPS rose only $0.78 to $0.82. There is no guidance and no consensus in the text, so this is mildly positive.
Reg FD notice of a November investor day and a cosmetic segment rename with no change to composition or financials; no numbers, so near zero with a faint positive for the investor-day announcement.
Routine amend-and-extend of an undrawn $500m revolver, maturity pushed to 2031 on the same size and terms. Not material.

Record adj EBITDA of $34.0m at a 31% margin, and the CEO says enterprise ARR growth accelerated again and expects that momentum to continue into Q3. Total ARR of $440.8m is not given against a prior period, and the release text carries no guidance and no consensus, so this is sized as a modest positive on tone and margin.

The board is expanded to add the founder of Lynrock Lake, an investment firm, whose recent boards (ON24, DSP Group) ended in sales. With a take-private proposal from the CEO in the background, that is a faint positive read. Otherwise a routine appointment.
Nasdaq deficiency notice for the late 10-K. It was expected after the 12b-25, but it confirms consolidation problems at an erratic microcap that has just done a reverse split. Mildly negative.

Formal filing of a 1-for-20 reverse split that was announced on Aug 13 and already effective on Aug 17, before this t0. Little new information, with a slight negative drift typical of post-split microcaps.

Closing of the Best Life acquisition announced on 07-27: $30m paid in USDT, $20m due within 90 days, plus earn-outs. It is a large cash commitment for an unrelated import-export business at a tiny AI company. The deal was already public, so the reaction is slight and negative.

The CFO resigns for retirement on three days' notice with no successor named, at a speculative microcap mid-pivot to AI data centers that has just raised equity. The no-disagreement language softens it, but it is still mildly negative.

Updates the share count to 502m after the offering priced and disclosed on Aug 11. The dilution was already known, and this only restates it, along with the overhang of 124m pre-funded and 400m other warrants.
Name change to Zone Frontier, already announced by press release on Aug 14, before this filing's t0, with the ticker unchanged. No new information.

Q4 headline 25% growth is flattered by Red Canary (organic ARR +20%, organic net new ARR +17%), Q4 FCF margin collapsed to 7% on a capex jump, and Q1 FY27 revenue guide of ~19% signals deceleration; no consensus in the text and the outlook is truncated, so sized on text alone, with a 3% layoff as a minor offset. No memory of the reaction.

Q2 comps turned negative (-2.1%) and the loss widened year on year; worse, Q3-to-date comps are -3.5% with back-to-school weak in the U.S., and the Q3 guide of $222-226M and EPS $0.00-0.10 points to a clear decline. No consensus in the text, so sized on the deteriorating trend in a small-cap retailer. No memory of the reaction.

The CFO is leaving after 19 years with no successor named, but he stays through the transition and the filing gives no sign of a dispute or anything to do with the numbers. That makes it a small negative on uncertainty. No memory of the reaction.

First Alloy Kore design win with the Daimler Truck/Volvo JV, adding over $100m to QNX royalty backlog and billed as the largest design win in QNX history; a meaningful validation of the QNX story for a retail-heavy, volatile name, but backlog is long-dated and not revenue, so a moderate positive rather than a large one.

Routine credit-agreement amendment: term A and revolver refinanced, revolver up $100m, maturity to 2031, margins cut 25bp, and the undrawn $2.1bn bridge terminated with nothing outstanding; mildly favourable terms and no new equity, so near zero.

Microcap takes $20m of secured 10% venture debt that starts amortizing in three months at $1.25-2.0m a month, with 1.45m warrants at $3.30 and a covenant cushion built on its ATM capacity, which signals continued ATM selling; funding removes near-term liquidity risk, but the structure reads as expensive and dilutive, so a moderate negative.
Routine bylaw amendment updating advance-notice disclosure requirements for Delaware case law, plus technical changes; no economic content.
Compensation-committee approval of award forms for performance RSUs tied to Hyve Solutions' three-year financials; routine, with at most a faint read that Hyve is being managed as a standalone unit.
Updated employment agreement for the continuing Chief Legal Officer ($670k salary, $1.5m equity); routine compensation disclosure with no bearing on value.
New EUR 650m European receivables securitization for a large IT distributor that already runs working-capital facilities; ordinary liquidity plumbing with customary terms, so zero.

June comps +8.8% total and +7.0% ex-gas/FX, with U.S. ex-gas +7.6% running above the 44-week +6.7% pace and digital +21.5%. That is an acceleration, which argues for a modest up move in a richly valued name. The dividend is unchanged and routine. The text gives no consensus bar, so the size rests on the comparison with the year-to-date pace.
Reg FD filing of an investor presentation, and the exhibit text holds no new numbers. This is routine, so it is scored zero on the text alone.

Annual-meeting vote count, filed five days after the meeting. Withhold votes on the common-stock directors were heavy (about 50% on Barge, about 34% on the other two). That shows shareholder discontent, but Class A holders control the board, so nothing changes in practice. Routine.

The company bought back 1.6% of its common shares from the founder's estate in a private deal at a 3% discount, using the existing authorization. The block is absorbed off-market, which is mildly accretive. Against that, the estate says it needs cash for its obligations, which points to more estate supply later. Small positive net.
